column1: # LSF accounting for one full Snakemake run of all 18 step rules, read out of
# `logs/lsf/<rule>.<jobid>.out`. This is the evidence behind the per-rule tiers
# in rules/common.smk, and tests/test_resources.py checks the tiers against it.
# Run: CCHMC BMICluster, 2026-09-09/10, PBMC multiome fixture (~11k cells),
# every rule submitted with the single `default` tier of the day (128000 MB,
# 16 slots where the rule asked for them).
# TWO CAVEATS, both load-bearing:
# 1. This run PREDATES the reproducibility pinning (it is the run whose
#    eRegulon count came out 86 against the driver's 74). Unpinned, BLAS thread
#    count follows the host's core count, which is why `max_threads` reaches
#    1661. Pinned runs should need the same memory or less, so these figures are
#    an upper bound for sizing -- but they have not been re-measured pinned.
# 2. `max_mem_mb` is LSF's figure for the whole process TREE, not one process.
#    R09 reports 152566 MB against a 128000 MB reservation and did not die,
#    because `-M` is enforced PER PROCESS. Read it as "this much RAM must exist
#    on the node", which is what `rusage[mem]` reserves -- not as a per-process
#    ceiling that was breached.
# 3. THE LAST TWO ROWS COME FROM A DIFFERENT RUN -- the 2026-09-11 rerun, which
#    is the first to include R19 and R20. Their `node` and `slots` are recorded
#    as `unknown` because the operator supplied the resource block without the
#    host line; nothing reads those two columns, and inventing a node name would
#    put a fact in this file that nobody measured.
#    That rerun requested 128000 MB for both, which is the PRE-I5 uniform tier
#    -- so it did NOT exercise the per-rule tiers. What a rule USED is
#    independent of what it reserved, so these figures size the tiers correctly
#    regardless; they just do not validate them.
# 4. R21_report's row is from the 2026-09-12 run, the first on I5's own tiers --
#    `Total Requested Memory: 4000.00 MB` matches the `4g` tier, confirming it.
#    Its node and slots are `unknown` for a STRUCTURAL reason, not a missing
#    paste: R21 renders the report, and LSF appends a job's accounting when the
#    job ENDS, so R21's own epilogue does not exist while R21 is running. It is
#    absent from the report's own Compute table for the same reason.
